abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Insulin-mediated microvascular perfusion was reduced in participants with T2D (-0.30 arbitrary perfusion units [APU]/mm Hg; P < 0.001) and in HFpEF with T2D (-0.32 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.004) compared with controls, whereas responses in HFpEF without T2D were not different from controls. Perfusion responses to sodium nitroprusside were reduced in T2D and HFpEF with T2D, while responses to acetylcholine were preserved. No statistically detectable interaction between HFpEF and T2D was observed. Sex did not modify the relationship between HFpEF and microvascular dysfunction, but exploratory sex-stratified analyses showed reduced insulin-mediated microvascular perfusion in T2D (mean difference: -0.30 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.020) and HFpEF + T2D (mean difference: -0.51 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.002) compared with controls.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Systemic microvascular dysfunction, particularly impaired insulin-mediated vasodilation, was observed in HFpEF. The observed abnormalities were predominantly present in participants with comorbid type 2 diabetes.

articles.conclusion: Systemic microvascular dysfunction, particularly impaired insulin-mediated vasodilation, was observed in HFpEF. The observed abnormalities were predominantly present in participants with comorbid type 2 diabetes.

articles.title: Tricuspid inflow E-wave velocity for the assessment of severe or greater tricuspid regurgitation: derivation and external validation of threshold values

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: Current guidelines include tricuspid inflow E-wave (>100 cm/s by pulsed-wave Doppler) as a semiquantitative criterion for diagnosing severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR), despite limited supporting evidence. We assessed its diagnostic performance for identifying severe or greater TR, deriving and externally validating practical thresholds.

abstract.label: METHODS AND RESULTS
abstract.text: Tricuspid inflow E-wave velocity was measured by pulsed-wave Doppler in consecutive patients with at least mild TR between December 2024 and February 2026. Among 178 patients (77±13 years, 65% women), TR was mild in 44, moderate in 61, severe in 44, massive in 15, and torrential in 14. Mean tricuspid E-wave velocity was 56±16 cm/s and increased with TR severity: 47±8, 50±10, 62±16, 67±13, and 77±21 cm/s for mild, moderate, severe, massive, and torrential TR. Only three patients had E-wave velocity >100 cm/s (one with severe and two with torrential TR). Using multiparametric echocardiographic grading as the reference standard, the >100 cm/s threshold showed 5.5% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and kappa 0.25 for severe or greater TR. As a continuous variable, E-wave velocity discriminated severe or greater TR with an AUC of 0.81. A lower threshold of 52 cm/s yielded 81% sensitivity and 67% specificity, whereas 47 cm/s provided 90% sensitivity and 43% specificity. External validation resulted in 94% sensitivity and 47% specificity.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The guideline-recommended threshold of >100 cm/s is highly insensitive for detecting severe or greater TR. Lower cut-offs, particularly 47 cm/s, may be useful for screening to trigger a comprehensive multiparametric assessment.

articles.conclusion: The guideline-recommended threshold of >100 cm/s is highly insensitive for detecting severe or greater TR. Lower cut-offs, particularly 47 cm/s, may be useful for screening to trigger a comprehensive multiparametric assessment.

articles.title: Electrical Storm Triggered by Conus Branch Occlusion During Elective Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Very Severe Aortic Stenosis: Rescue With Balloon Aortic Valvuloplasty Under Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstract.text: We report a case of very severe aortic stenosis (AS) in which side-branch occlusion during elective percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) precipitated life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias and hemodynamic collapse. The patient was a 72-year-old man with very severe AS who was scheduled to undergo a valve intervention. Preprocedural coronary angiography revealed a significant, newly developed stenosis in the right coronary artery, and an elective PCI was performed prior to valve treatment. Following intravascular lithotripsy and drug-eluting stent implantation, occlusion of the conus branch occurred, triggering recurrent ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation. Despite initiation of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and intra-aortic balloon pump support, the patient's hemodynamic status did not improve. Because excessive afterload due to very severe AS was considered the principal pathophysiological mechanism, emergency balloon aortic valvuloplasty was performed. This resulted in rapid hemodynamic stabilization and complete resolution of ventricular arrhythmias. This case illustrates that even a minor side-branch occlusion during PCI can lead to catastrophic outcomes in patients with very severe AS. Furthermore, it highlights that mechanical circulatory support alone may be insufficient, and that prompt relief of valvular obstruction is essential. Careful consideration of the indications and sequence of coronary intervention through discussions with a heart team is warranted for patients with very severe AS.

articles.title: Pretransplant Sensitization and Outcomes Across Isolated Heart, Heart-Kidney, and Heart-Liver Transplantation

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: High pretransplant sensitization, assessed by calculated panel-reactive antibody (cPRA), is a recognized immunologic risk factor in heart transplantation. Whether its significance differs across isolated heart transplantation (HT), simultaneous heart-kidney transplantation (SHKT), and combined heart-liver transplantation (CHLT) remains unclear.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using the UNOS thoracic registry, we identified adult primary isolated HT, SHKT, and CHLT recipients from January 2015 to June 2024. High sensitization was defined as cPRA ≥50%. Outcomes included rejection, 1-year graft failure, and 1- and 3-year mortality. Multivariable analyses were cohort-specific.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 20,085 isolated HT, 2,045 SHKT, and 342 CHLT recipients, high cPRA was present in 9.8%, 11.7%, and 18.1%, respectively. High cPRA was associated with treated rejection within 1 year after isolated HT (adjusted OR, 1.25; 95% CI, 1.09-1.43) and rejection before discharge after SHKT (adjusted OR, 1.87; 95% CI, 1.18-2.96). High cPRA was also modestly associated with 3-year mortality after isolated HT (adjusted HR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.01-1.31), but was not associated with 1-year graft failure or mortality in any group. No significant association with rejection, graft failure, or mortality was observed after CHLT. Interaction testing did not show significant effect modification.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The clinical significance of pretransplant sensitization varied by transplant type, outcome, and follow-up horizon. High cPRA identified rejection-related risk after isolated HT and SHKT and a modest longer-term mortality signal after isolated HT, supporting a context-dependent interpretation of cPRA in isolated and multi-organ heart transplantation.

articles.conclusion: The clinical significance of pretransplant sensitization varied by transplant type, outcome, and follow-up horizon. High cPRA identified rejection-related risk after isolated HT and SHKT and a modest longer-term mortality signal after isolated HT, supporting a context-dependent interpretation of cPRA in isolated and multi-organ heart transplantation.

articles.title: Advanced Age in Acute Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock by Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Status

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a leading cause of in-hospital mortality in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Although advanced age is associated with worse outcomes, associations across out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) strata remain incompletely characterized.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The objective of the study was to evaluate the association between octogenarian status and in-hospital mortality in patients with AMI-related CS (AMI-CS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and to examine this association in analyses stratified by OHCA status.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed patients with AMI-CS enrolled in the multicenter Kanagawa-ACuTe cardIoVascular rEgistry who underwent PCI. Octogenarian status (≥80 years) was the primary exposure. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations with in-hospital mortality, with additional analyses stratified by OHCA status.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 658 patients, 177 (26.9%) were octogenarians, and 279 (42.4%) died during hospitalization. Octogenarian status was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR: 2.14; 95% CI: 1.32-3.48; P = 0.002). In stratified analyses, octogenarian status was associated with higher mortality among patients without OHCA, whereas no statistically significant association was observed among those with OHCA. The interaction between octogenarian status and OHCA was not statistically significant (P for interaction = 0.422). Higher heart rate, unmeasurable heart rate, higher serum creatinine, and lower serum albumin were independently associated with mortality.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In patients with AMI-CS undergoing PCI, octogenarian status was independently associated with in-hospital mortality. Although estimates differed numerically across OHCA strata, the interaction was not statistically significant, precluding a conclusion that the association differed according to OHCA status. These stratified findings should therefore be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Chronological age should be considered within a comprehensive clinical assessment rather than in isolation.

articles.conclusion: In patients with AMI-CS undergoing PCI, octogenarian status was independently associated with in-hospital mortality. Although estimates differed numerically across OHCA strata, the interaction was not statistically significant, precluding a conclusion that the association differed according to OHCA status. These stratified findings should therefore be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Chronological age should be considered within a comprehensive clinical assessment rather than in isolation.

articles.title: Pulmonary arterial hypertension in adult congenital heart disease: prevalence, outcomes and treatment patterns

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive, life-threatening complication of congenital heart disease (CHD). We aimed to determine the burden of clinically relevant PAH in a well-characterised adult CHD population.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study included 35 235 adult CHD patients from the Australian National CHD Registry, of whom 392 had clinically significant PAH (mean±sd age 43.4±13.9) (prevalence 1.11%). We prospectively defined clinically significant PAH as 1) prescription of PAH-specific therapy and/or 2) known Eisenmenger syndrome. 330 patients (84.2%) received PAH pharmacotherapy during the study period and 193 patients (49.2%) had Eisenmenger syndrome, 62 (32.1%) of whom were untreated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: During the study period, 141 (36.0%) patients died, PAH treatment was associated with a numerically lower risk of mortality (hazard ratio (HR) 0.74, 95% CI 0.49-1.11; p=0.22). Patients with moderate complexity CHD had a significantly higher risk of death than the mild group (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.08-2.92; p=0.023), whilst severe complexity patients had >2.5 times the risk of death (p<0.001). At last follow-up, 211 (63.9%) of treated patients were prescribed monotherapy, 90 (27.3%) dual and 29 (8.8%) triple therapy. From initial treatment to last follow-up, 123 (37.3%) of the treated group had switched therapy, 100 (30.3%) died, 75 (22.7%) continued their initial pharmacotherapy, 25 (7.6%) added additional drugs and seven (2.1%) underwent transplantation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Approximately 1.11% of a large adult CHD population had clinically significant PAH. Mortality is high (6.9% at age 30 years, 35.7% at age 50 years) and treatment has shifted towards increased utilisation of combination therapy.

articles.conclusion: Approximately 1.11% of a large adult CHD population had clinically significant PAH. Mortality is high (6.9% at age 30 years, 35.7% at age 50 years) and treatment has shifted towards increased utilisation of combination therapy.

articles.title: Simultaneous Aortic and Mitral Valve-in-Valve Replacement Using Balloon-Expandable MyVal Valves With Bioprosthetic Valve Fracture
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstract.text: Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement and mitral valve replacement have proved to be a viable alternative to redo surgery in patients who have bioprosthetic valve dysfunction. There is a large subgroup of patients who undergo double valve replacement with bioprosthetic valves, especially in patients with rheumatic heart disease. Failure of these bioprosthetic valves would require a transcatheter management strategy. Transcatheter double valve replacement (TDVR) in these complex cases would require careful evaluation and planning of valve sizing, aortomitral interactions, access, and residual gradients. A 73-year-old man with rheumatic heart disease and prior double bioprosthetic valve replacement in 2014 presented with New York Heart Association class (NYHA) III dyspnea and exertional pre-syncope. He had severe stenosis of a 19 mm Perimount Magna aortic bioprosthesis and a 27 mm Perimount Magna mitral bioprosthesis, with pulmonary hypertension. Computed tomography demonstrated suitable anatomy for transcatheter valve-in-valve treatment. He underwent successful TDVR with a 20 mm MyVal balloon-expandable in the aortic position, followed by a post-implantation valve fracture, and a 27.5 mm MyVal transseptally in the mitral position. The final mean gradients were 15 mmHg across the aortic valve and 6 mmHg across the mitral valve at discharge. At 1-year follow-up, the patient remained clinically well without an increase in valve gradients. Simultaneous transcatheter aortic and mitral valve-in-valve replacement can be performed successfully in selected high-risk patients after meticulous multimodality planning. In patients with a small surgical aortic bioprosthesis, intentional bioprosthetic valve fracture may be an important adjunct to optimize post-implantation hemodynamics. This report highlights the complexity of procedural planning for bioprosthetic valve fracture in a small aortic valve, ensuring optimal hemodynamics and the safety and durability of the Myval transcatheter heart valve in challenging and complex procedures like TDVR.

articles.title: Internal Mammary Artery Bypass Graft Dissection Mimicking Atherosclerotic Stenosis: Optical Coherence Tomography to Guide Stent Deferral
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstract.text: Angiographic narrowing of a left internal mammary artery (LIMA) bypass graft does not always reflect atherosclerotic progression. Chronic or spontaneous LIMA graft dissection may be identified using optical coherence tomography (OCT). A patient with severe multivessel coronary disease and a history of coronary stenting and triple coronary artery bypass grafting presented with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Coronary angiography demonstrated critical left main-left circumflex disease, extensive left anterior descending artery in-stent restenosis, an occluded venous graft, and eccentric mid-LIMA narrowing. Urgent native-vessel revascularization restored Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) grade 3 flow and relieved the patient's symptoms. During staged LIMA assessment 6 days later, OCT was performed using a Dragonfly OpStar imaging catheter. OCT identified the entry of a longitudinal intimal flap separating the true and false lumens over a long segment, without significant atherosclerosis in the imaged segment. The operators interpreted this "double-barrel" configuration as a nonobstructive dissection of presumed chronicity. Preserved LIMA flow and clinical stability supported stent deferral; the patient remained asymptomatic and with preserved ejection fraction at the 2-month follow-up visit. This report offers important lessons for interventionalists: intravascular imaging can distinguish dissection from apparent atherosclerotic stenosis and significantly drive further management. Inadvertent false-lumen stenting could expand the false channel, compress the true lumen, and compromise graft perfusion. OCT clearly elucidated lesion morphology and supported clinical restraint; however, it did not independently establish dissection age or an exact mechanism of dissection.

articles.title: 293-Day Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Support as a Bridge to Transplantation in Refractory Heart Failure

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) is widely used as temporary mechanical circulatory support in patients with refractory heart failure complicated by cardiogenic shock. However, its use is generally limited to short-term therapy because of device-related complications.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 57-year-old man with idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy receiving guideline-directed medical therapy and cardiac resynchronization therapy with defibrillation developed cardiogenic shock refractory to inotropic therapy, requiring IABP implantation. Mechanical circulatory support was maintained for 293 days, including 291 days as a bridge to heart transplantation and 2 days after transplantation.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case demonstrates that prolonged IABP support is feasible when combined with transition to a left subclavian approach, serial device replacement, and meticulous multidisciplinary management.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: In carefully selected patients, prolonged IABP support, combined with individualized device management and multidisciplinary care, may provide sustained clinical stabilization and serve as an effective bridge to heart transplantation.

articles.title: On-Pump Beating-Heart Redo Mitral Valve Surgery: A Personalized, Risk-Adapted Surgical Strategy for Plug-Induced Hemolysis

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Severe mechanical hemolysis following the use of a paravalvular leak occluder plug is a challenging complication, particularly for patients with multiple comorbidities who face prohibitive risks with repeat surgery.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 63-year-old multimorbid man with end-stage renal disease presented with severe microangiopathic hemolytic anemia after transcatheter paravalvular leak closure. Ten months earlier, he had undergone aortic and mitral valve replacements and coronary bypass, complicated by a difficult recovery requiring temporary mechanical circulatory support with an Impella. Now, to minimize the operative risk and avoid the difficult postoperative course experienced after the previous surgery requiring mechanical circulatory support, a modified, infrequent surgical strategy was used: On-pump, beating-heart redo mitral valve replacement with extraction of the occluder plug. It successfully circumvented global myocardial ischemia and simplified complex redo surgery. Postoperatively, the hematologic parameters normalized within days.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This personalized, risk-adapted surgical strategy mitigates operative risk in a high-risk patient, achieving rapid, definitive resolution of hemolytic anemia.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: Eliminating the source of mechanical hemolysis results in rapid normalization of laboratory parameters within days. On-pump beating-heart surgery is a valuable strategy to simplify complex redo procedures while minimizing high perioperative risk.

articles.title: External Validation of a Risk Score Assessment for Pediatric Ventricular Assist Device Mortality
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstract.text: The ACTION score was internally validated to predict mortality after pediatric ventricular assist device (VAD) placement. This study aims to externally validate the ACTION score and compare its performance to the INTERMACS profile for prediction of mortality in pediatric VAD candidates. The publicly available Pedimacs dataset (531 patients) was used for external validation. The Pedimacs dataset as well as a contemporary ACTION dataset (1,304 patients) were used to compare the performance of the ACTION score and INTERMACS profile. A statistically significant linear trend in the proportion of death across increasing ACTION scores (p < 0.0001) was observed in the Pedimacs dataset, with a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve demonstrating an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.71. Both the ACTION score and the INTERMACS profile demonstrated a significant linear trend in the proportion of death across scores in the ACTION dataset. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated an AUC of 0.71 and 0.58 for the ACTION score and INTERMACS profile, respectively. The ACTION score is externally validated with the Pedimacs dataset and is a fair predictor of mortality. The ACTION score performed better than the INTERMACS profile in predicting mortality using both historical Pedimacs data and contemporary ACTION data.

articles.title: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial of a Digital Health Intervention for Medication Optimization in Heart Failure: The ENGAGE-HF Trial Outcomes

abstract.text: Background: Despite clear evidence that guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) significantly reduces mortality and hospitalizations in patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced and mildly reduced ejection fraction, real-world implementation remains suboptimal. Digital health interventions may promote GDMT titration after hospital discharge. Methods: The ENGAGE-HF trial was a multicenter, two-arm, open-label, randomized controlled trial across three academic centers, funded by the AHA Strategically Focused Research Network (SFRN) for Health Technology and Innovation. Patients recently hospitalized with HF, with or without a primary hospital diagnosis of HF, and LVEF <50% receiving suboptimal GDMT were randomized 1:1 to either the ENGAGE-HF app or usual care for 90 days. The ENGAGE-HF intervention consisted of a patient-facing mobile app and a clinician dashboard overseen by study coordinators. The primary outcome was the Medication Optimization Score (MOS, scale 0-100%) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes were individual GDMT therapies and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score at 90 days. Results: A total of 134 participants were randomized. At 90 days, the adjusted MOS was significantly higher in the ENGAGE-HF group compared to the control group (83.7% vs. 74.0%, p = 0.010). Results remained consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses. Overall prescribing prevalence increased more in the ENGAGE-HF group for MRAs (+15.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points) and SGLT2 inhibitors (+10.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points). Furthermore, the ENGAGE-HF group demonstrated greater increases in achieving target doses for ARNI (+18.8% vs. +6.3%) and beta-blockers (+8.5% vs. +0.6%). KCCQ-23 CSS at 90 days was 75.2 (SE 2.6) in the intervention group versus 72.2 (SE 2.6) in the control group (between-group p = 0.40). Conclusions: ENGAGE-HF, a digital health intervention that integrates remote monitoring, patient engagement, and clinical decision support, significantly improved GDMT optimization at 90 days compared with usual care among patients with HF. Registration: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov Unique Identifier: NCT06750549.

articles.title: Prehospital Extracorporeal Life Support in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) with the use of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation can be performed to establish reperfusion. Data comparing prehospital ECPR with conventional care regarding survival until hospital discharge among patients who are 50 years of age or younger with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest are limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In a nationwide, nonrandomized study conducted in the Netherlands, we evaluated the outcomes in young adults who were attended by Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (HEMS) that were equipped to deliver prehospital ECPR (intervention group) as compared with those attended by HEMS without ECPR capability (conventional group). The primary outcome was survival until hospital discharge.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 144 patients were included in the intervention group, and 87 were included in the conventional group. In the intervention group, 57 of 144 patients (40%) survived until hospital discharge, as compared with 17 of 87 patients (20%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 2.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.59 to 4.66; P = 0.002). At 6 months, a favorable neurologic outcome was reported in 51 of 141 patients (36%) in the intervention group and in 11 of 85 patients (13%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 4.22; 95% CI, 2.82 to 6.32). There were 32 adverse events in the intervention group and 11 in the conventional group.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among patients who were 50 years of age or younger with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, incorporating ECPR into HEMS was associated with improved survival until hospital discharge, as compared with conventional care. (Funded by the Dutch Ministry of Health; OnScene ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04620070.).

articles.conclusion: Among patients who were 50 years of age or younger with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, incorporating ECPR into HEMS was associated with improved survival until hospital discharge, as compared with conventional care. (Funded by the Dutch Ministry of Health; OnScene ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04620070.).

articles.title: Natural Language Processing for the Adjudication of Heart Failure with Reduced and Preserved Ejection Fraction in the Electronic Health Record

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Administrative billing codes commonly misclassify complex diseases like heart failure (HF) in the electronic health record (EHR). Artificial intelligence (AI) approaches, including natural language processing (NLP), may improve disease adjudication.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: We validated an existing NLP model and specifically examined accuracy across HF subtypes (preserved vs reduced ejection fraction: HFpEF, EF ≥50%; HFrEF, EF <50%) in an EHR-based sample.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We identified individuals who sought primary care between 2004-2014 at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. Incident HF hospitalizations were identified using International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes, and gold-standard HF adjudication was performed in 500 random cases. We applied a preexisting NLP model to classify each case and then further fine-tuned the model. We calculated diagnostic metrics for overall HF and by subtype.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 156,409 individuals, 5014 incident HF cases were identified. The fine-tuned NLP model outperformed primary ICD codes, yielding a superior kappa (0.73 vs 0.49), negative predictive value (93% vs 73%), and sensitivity (89% vs 52%), with similar positive predictive value (79% vs 87%) and specificity (86% vs 94%). Notably, NLP performance was robust across HF subtypes, whereas primary ICD codes had worse performance for identification of HFpEF. When applied to the full cohort, NLP identified 84% more HFrEF and 99% more HFpEF candidate cases than primary ICD codes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: NLP accurately classifies HF cases across subtypes, with improved accuracy after fine-tuning. AI-based approaches represent a critical opportunity to improve disease ascertainment at scale, nearly doubling the number of HF cases identified in the EHR.

articles.conclusion: NLP accurately classifies HF cases across subtypes, with improved accuracy after fine-tuning. AI-based approaches represent a critical opportunity to improve disease ascertainment at scale, nearly doubling the number of HF cases identified in the EHR.

articles.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Understand Reasons for SGLT2 Nontreatment Among Patients With Heart Failure

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Many patients with heart failure (HF) and a guideline indication for sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) do not receive a prescription, but the reasons behind this are unclear. This study optimizes an large language model framework to identify reasons for the lack of SGLT2i prescriptions.

abstract.label: METHODS AND RESULTS
abstract.text: We extracted clinical notes for patients >18 years old with a first HF diagnosis identified by International Classification of Diseases, 10th edition, code seen in cardiology clinics between August 10, 2021, and March 1, 2025. Five annotators labeled reasons for SGLT2i nonprescription (the test set); the remaining unlabeled notes served as the inference set. Using both zero-shot (prompts do not include examples) and few-shot prompting techniques, we compared 2 large language models from OpenAI on their ability to classify the documented reason for nonprescription into 1 of 6 themes and 1 of 14 subthemes. We identified 599 HF patients (with 1123 notes), with an average age of 71 years and predominantly having HF with preserved ejection fraction. We used 313 labeled and 705 unlabeled notes as the test and inference sets, respectively, for a total set of 1018 notes. GPT-o1 outperformed GPT-4o and was 84.7% accurate (95% confidence interval 80.2%-88.5%) in identifying theme reasons for SGLT2i nonprescription. The most frequent theme was physician-attributed factors (n = 292 notes [28.7%]), among the total set. Physician deferral to a future visit (n = 157 notes [15.4%]) and the physician perceiving the patient to be at low risk or unlikely to benefit (n = 75 [7.4%]) were the most prevalent subthemes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: We optimized a large language model to accurately discriminate reasons for not prescribing SGLT2is from clinical notes. When a reason for SGLT2i nonprescription was documented, delayed initiation of SGLT2i and physician perception of patients as being at low risk were the most common reasons, offering valuable insight to improve guideline-indicated SGLT2i prescription.

articles.title: Electrocardiogram-based Artificial Intelligence to Predict Incident Heart Failure With Preserved vs Reduced Ejection Fraction

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Heart failure is classically divided into 2 subtypes based on the ejection fraction (EF): HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), each with varying risk-mitigation strategies. Electrocardiogram-based artificial intelligence (AI) may facilitate HF subtype-specific risk prediction, enabling tailored prevention.

abstract.label: METHODS AND RESULTS
abstract.text: Based on a previously validated HF-prediction architecture, we developed an ECG-based AI model to predict 10-year risk of incident HFrEF (LVEF <50%) vs HFpEF (LVEF ≥50%) (Electrocardiogram to Heart Failure Subtype, ECG2HF-Subtype). ECG2HF-Subtype was developed in 98,190 individuals at Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH) and validated in 3 test sets: MGH, Brigham and Women's Hospital (BWH), and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC) among individuals without prior HF. HF was identified by using a validated natural language processing model, and subtypes were classified by LVEF proximate to incident HF. Discrimination was quantified using time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and average precision (AP), with comparisons to age and sex, and a multinomial logistic regression classifier, including variables in the Predicting Risk of cardiovascular disease EVENTs (PREVENT-HF) equations. In aggregate, models were evaluated in MGH (n = 16,739, ages 56 ± 17, 54% women), BWH (n = 75,195, 56 ± 16, 59%), and BIDMC (n = 30,133, 56 ± 17, 54%). ECG2HF-Subtype consistently discriminated incident HFrEF (MGH 10-year AUROC 0.89 [0.86-0.91], 10-year AP: 0.11 [95%CI 0.09-0.15], cumulative incidence 1.73%; BWH: 0.88 [0.87-0.89], 0.13 [0.11-0.14], 2.23%; BIDMC: 0.88 [0.86-0.89], 0.14 [0.12-0.17], 2.19%), and HFpEF events (MGH 10-year AUROC 0.83 [0.81-0.85], 10-year AP: 0.10 [95% CI 0.09-0.13], cumulative incidence 3.17%; BWH: 0.79 [0.77-0.80], 0.06 [0.06-0.07], 2.75%; BIDMC: 0.81 [0.80-0.82], 0.10 [0.09-0.12], 3.49%), with consistently greater AUROC vs age and sex. When compared to PREVENT-HF variables, ECG2HF-Subtypes had favorable discrimination of HFrEF (eg, 10-year AUROC in MGH+BWH 0.86 [0.84-0.88] vs 0.78 [0.76-0.80]), and modestly lower for HFpEF (10-year AUROC in MGH+BWH 0.78 [0.76-0.80] vs 0.81 [0.79-0.82]).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: By predicting the risk of HFpEF and HFrEF, AI-enabled ECG analysis may enable targeted prevention to reduce HF-related morbidity.

articles.conclusion: By predicting the risk of HFpEF and HFrEF, AI-enabled ECG analysis may enable targeted prevention to reduce HF-related morbidity.
